title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
authors: Seth Karten, Alex L. Zhang, Kevin Thomas, Sebastian Müller, Elie Bakouch, Daniel Auras, Mika Senghaas, Fares Obeid, Konstantin Dunas, Johannes Hagemann, Sami Jaghouar
lab: Prime Intellect, with Princeton University and MIT (correspondence: Seth Karten, Alex L. Zhang)
date: 24 August 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version so far; the HTML says first published 5 August 2026, the day of the launch blog post)

code.title: PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent, MIT licence
code.time: 20 min for the README and entry path
code.note: The harness itself, under the MIT licence, installable with one command; it began as a fork of Mario Zechner's pi (pi-mono) coding agent and was ported from TypeScript to Rust on 30 September 2026, after the paper. No evaluation configurations, traces or benchmark adapters are in the repository; the one public trace is the ARC-AGI-3 scorecard linked from the blog

takeaway: Open-source harness built on a four-level state hierarchy (weights, context, persistent IPython REPL plus live subagents, disk history) with a Recursive Language Model abstraction, a Continual Harness that versions prompts/memories/skills/subagent specs across trajectories, and direct agent-to-agent messaging; lifts ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 from 30% to 95.5%, sustains 85.5-hour nanoGPT speedruns and 7-day Factorio runs, and reports that models are not trained to use most of what it offers.
verdict: Believe the harness: it is released, MIT-licensed, and its one public ARC-AGI-3 run rescores to exactly the 95.24% it claims. Do not read "30% to 95.5%" as a measured harness effect: the 30% is a different harness's published score, 95.5% is the best of three runs on the easier public game set, where community harnesses had already scored 99 to 100%, and every other comparison is one run without error bars, mostly inside the noise.

headline.k: ARC-AGI-3 public set with Opus 5 inside Prime Agent: the best of three runs (95.0, 95.2, 95.5); the released median run rescores to 95.24%
headline.d: the "30%" it is set against is Opus 5 in the official ARC harness, not a run of this paper

headline.k: Table 1 model pairs where Prime Agent's point estimate is higher than the other harness's; 13 of the 27 gaps are under 0.02
headline.d: single runs, no intervals; this page counts

headline.k: spawned by the root in a 7-day Factorio run (at most 7 at once) that completed 24 of 196 technologies on 23.4M output tokens
headline.d: the same section reports the agent saving a resource-spawning cheat as a skill

resources.t: Prime Agent: A self-improving RLM agent
resources.n: the launch post: the TUI and Agents View, the rlm and Continual Harness code, the three ARC runs (95.0, 95.2, 95.5) with Best@3 99.97%, the earlier version of Table 1, and the Factorio cheating footage. Acknowledges that Prime Agent is built on pi.
every game and level of the median run, with the action replays; the data behind this page's rescoring tab.

resources.t: ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence
resources.n: the benchmark: how RHAE scores a level against the upper-median human, why the public set is easier, and why the official leaderboard runs without any harness.
self-reported harness results on the ARC-AGI-3 public set, which ARC Prize does not verify; Prime Agent is not listed, its predecessor Continual Harness is (20.5%).
the RLM abstraction Prime Agent implements: context held as a variable in a REPL and the model calling itself on parts of it; the source of OOLONG-Pairs.

resources.t: Continual Harness: online adaptation for self-improving foundation agents
resources.n: the typed, versioned prompts, memories, skills and subagents with a Refiner, by the same first author; Prime Agent folds it in as the L3 layer.

resources.t: pi (pi-mono): the coding agent Prime Agent was forked from
resources.n: the upstream TypeScript agent; the GLM-5.2 column of Table 1 compares Prime Agent with this, so it is a fork against its own base.

resources.t: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
resources.n: the other ARC-AGI-3 harness result of that fortnight: Opus 5 from 30% to 100% inside Nvidia's Agentic Variation Operators.
the Python observation and action interface the Factorio runs use, and its production-score metric.

kb.t: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a $15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
kb.n: the opposite design from the same fortnight: a checked state-machine runbook around a fixed agent, where Prime Agent hands the model a REPL and subagents. Its page finds the same pattern of a benchmark-tuned upper bound.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: the general test of what Continual Harness does: when a model refines its own harness from feedback, the score it can see moved the same way as the held-out score in only 34 of 64 version changes.

kb.t: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
kb.n: the training-side answer to Prime Agent's closing claim that models are not trained to use their harness: it turns harness traffic into a training curriculum.

kb.t: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
kb.n: complementary: Prime Agent hands a rich harness to an untrained model; JIT-Agent trains a 27B model to write the harness for each task.

kb.t: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
kb.n: Continual Harness generalises SKILL.md from procedures to prompts, memories and subagent specifications, and inherits the misapplication failure that paper measured.
the issue that added this paper to the knowledge base, with JIT-Agent, WikiSkill and Apodex 1.1, under "harness scaling became a research programme".
the week before: Nvidia's Agentic Variation Operators result (Opus 5, 30% to 100% on ARC-AGI-3) and StateM.

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: a later attempt to keep self-editing harnesses from overfitting, the risk Prime Agent's refinement loop runs.

topics.n: harness scaling and harness engineering, where this paper is one of the main results.
ARC-AGI-3, OOLONG, LongBench v2 and the long-horizon benchmarks of Table 1.
the open-source agent systems Prime Agent is compared with (Claude Code, Codex, pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode, Kimi-Code).
reward hacking: the Factorio specification exploit belongs with that material, and model-harness co-training is the paper's proposed next step.
